mappings.note: Joint classification (LO-1) carried across into engineering: three robot joints have to be specified from the human analogue. C5.3 is cited for that transfer of a scientific principle into another curricular area; C-5.3-LO-2 is not, because nothing about fitness or tissue condition is at stake.
Picks the neuron process whose shape matches a direction of signal flow (long single axon carries away, branched dendrites receive). Structure-to-function of one cell part.

The role bone plays in the body - shielding heart and lungs - with the distractors offering other real skeletal roles. Not C-4.2-LO-4: the rib cage is treated as a functioning structure, not as a rung on the organisation ladder.
Four statements, each pairing a joint type with its permitted movement - hinge, ball and socket, pivot, fixed. Exactly the joint-types clause of LO-1 and nothing more.

Three muscle types have to be told apart from micrographs, which is LO-1; C-4.2-LO-2 because the stem makes the correlation between cellular architecture and physiological role the explicit basis of the choice.

Shoulder rotation identified as ball and socket (LO-1), asked inside an athlete's warm-up. The activity framing is what admits C-5.3-LO-2 here while the plain anatomical joint items in this part stay on LO-1 alone.

Mechanical models used purely as pictures of a ball-and-socket and a hinge, to be placed at the right anatomical sites. No design problem is posed, so unlike the robot item this one does not take C5.3.
Classifies the skull-to-vertebra articulation from a movement cue (shaking the head 'no'), which is the joint-types clause of LO-1.

Assertion is the immobility of cranial bones and the reason is the fixed joint, so LO-1 leads; C-4.2-LO-3 second because the reason also has to be judged on the protective role that immobility serves.
Names the tissue that cushions and flexes between vertebrae - the role of cartilage in the body. C-5.3-LO-2 withheld: the stem is anatomical, with no physical-activity or fitness framing.
A definition of tissue set explicitly in the multicellular context, with division of labour as the point - the level-of-organisation outcome.
Explicitly plant versus animal, the first discrimination in LO-1; C-4.2-LO-2 for the reasoning step from wall rigidity to upright support in a fixed organism.
Plant growth localised to dividing regions against uniform animal growth: a plant/animal contrast that rests on the meristematic tissue idea, both of them clauses of LO-1.
Locates apical meristem and states what that location achieves (increase in length) - role of a tissue in the plant. Not LO-6: no experiment is performed or interpreted here.
Straight statement of what lateral meristem does, matching the role outcome. Companion to the apical-meristem item above, which asks location rather than function.
The 2-mark twin of the hedge MCQ in part 3, and mapped more narrowly: with no options there is no permanent-tissue lure, so only the role of intercalary meristem is scored and LO-1 drops out.

Defines the process that converts meristematic cells into permanent tissue, the same call made on the differentiation MCQ in part 2. LO-1 is the nearest home; the frame has no outcome for differentiation as such.
Asks for a cell property, and every property in the answer is one that enables continuous division - structure serving function. No comparison with permanent tissue is required.
Role recall for stomata within the epidermis. C3.2 is kept for items where the exchange or transport process has to be reasoned through, not merely named.

The answer runs from a structural modification (large air cavities) to the property it confers (buoyancy), so structure-to-function. Split from the aerenchyma MCQ in part 2, where the tissue had to be named from the function alone (C-4.2-LO-3).

A direct structural comparison of collenchyma and sclerenchyma, which LO-1 names. C-4.2-LO-2 withheld deliberately: the question stops at the structural difference and never asks what either structure achieves.
Listing the cell types that make up phloem is the substance of both the simple/complex and the xylem/phloem discriminations in LO-1. No function is requested, so the role outcome is not cited.
Asks what epithelium does for the animal body - covering, lining, restricting water loss and germ entry. Role outcome, with no structural feature required.

Asks what would be observed structurally (a single layer of tall columnar cells) and why that suits absorption. Observation-of-structure, so C-4.2-LO-2 rather than the role outcome used for the general epithelium item.
Contrasts the matrix of two connective tissues, hard and calcified against fluid plasma. Structural comparison; LO-1 cannot take it because bone-versus-blood is not among the pairs it lists.
